findings.title: Plugin request completion log no longer includes traceID
findings.body: The old logRequest appended traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) to the 'Plugin Request Completed' log entry. That block was removed, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (instrumentContext) does not add traceID to the contextual attributes either. Nothing in this diff puts the trace ID into the log record, so completed plugin requests lose log-to-trace correlation for data egress logs. Either add traceID to the contextual attributes in instrumentContext or keep the field in logRequest.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a detached logger, so recorded calls are lost
findings.body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a fresh logger whose calls are never recorded on the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so with this fake the Info call goes to a throwaway logger and the parent's InfoLogs.Calls stays 0. Any test asserting on the fake's InfoLogs after exercising LoggerMiddleware will see no calls and fail, or will be unable to verify that the request was logged. FromContext should return f (or otherwise share the recorded state) so the fake captures the call.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently depends on this middleware being outer to it; no tests cover either
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware no longer adds pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID or uname itself. It relies on this middleware running before it so that m.logger.FromContext(ctx) returns those attributes. The only enforcement is the list order in pluginsintegration.go. If the order changes, or LoggerMiddleware is used without this middleware, completed-request logs silently lose these fields with no error. The doc note that the instrumentation middleware had to sit at the top of the stack was removed with the rename and not replaced here. No test covers ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and none checks that the attributes reach the emitted log record.
